problem: Most ObjectNav agents cannot ask for external help and search the whole space. Prior ask-for-help work rarely handles a teacher that is sometimes absent, and has no principled way to judge whether a query was well timed.
motivation: Asking is often more efficient than exhaustive search, but a real teacher is not always present, so an agent must not become over-reliant on feedback. The paper therefore trains the agent to ask via RL and adds a way to evaluate the timing of its queries.
key_idea: Add an 'ask' action to an RL ObjectNav policy that returns ground-truth object-in-view segmentation, train it with a semi-present-teacher curriculum for robustness, and assess query quality with a lower-bound uncertainty measure over goal location.
insight: An agent trained with an always-present teacher fails on nearly all episodes when the teacher is absent (e.g. Both Unseen SR 0.0, Seen SR 4.8), so it is over-reliant. Mixing in 25% or 75% teacher-present episodes restores baseline-level SR without teacher and still gains with a teacher. The uncertainty metric shows the always-present agent almost never asks consecutively (0.3%) and its asks reduce uncertainty more than navigation does, but vapid and insignificant asks remain high, partly because the metric assumes perfect memory.
method: Ask action: an extra discrete action in the PPO policy; when taken, the agent receives an object-in-view observation (binary GT segmentation mask of the target in the current view).

Architecture: pretrained ResNet-18 encodes RGB-D, target object is text-embedded, all are fed through a GRU into a 2x256 ReLU actor-critic with PPO; reward +10 on success, -0.01 per step; implemented in AllenAct.
Semi-present teacher curriculum: the teacher is present in eta% of training episodes (25% or 75%), and the agent gets a teacher-present flag; feedback is only available when present.

Uncertainty lower bound: a likelihood map Phi over 3D positions starts at 1 everywhere; lambda = sum(Phi) - max(Phi). Navigation reduces likelihood in seen regions with a piecewise-linear distance decay (alpha=1m, beta=2m); ask reduces it without decay.

Ask-quality metrics: percentage of ask actions, average uncertainty decrease per ask, and counts of consecutive, vapid (uncertainty <10% of start) and statistically insignificant (decrease < gamma=2.0) asks.
Feedback variants: binary in-view signal, noisy segmentation at eval (scaling 0.6-1.0, boundary jitter ±5px), and natural-language feedback (colour, near/far, position in frame) encoded with RoBERTa.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (pretrained) + GRU + PPO actor-critic MLP, trained from scratch for the policy; RoBERTa for the language variant
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR, 10 kitchen scenes, 5 object types (apple, bowl, potato, soap bottle, dish sponge), 10M steps; test on 5 unseen kitchen scenes and 2 unseen objects (cup, bread)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus target object category embedding, teacher-present flag, and object-in-view GT segmentation upon ask
setting.action_space: discrete: rotate left/right (90°), move forward 0.25m, look up/down (30°), stop, ask
setting.privileged: Ground-truth object segmentation used as teacher feedback on ask; GT object positions used for uncertainty evaluation

numbers_note: Custom AI2-THOR kitchen ObjectNav with randomized object placement and no standard benchmark or official split; 'val' is used for the held-out seen/unseen test cases. Baseline (no ask, no teacher) Both Seen SR 35.2 / SPL 24.1, Both Unseen SR 11.9 / SPL 7.7.
results: With a present teacher, the always-present-teacher agent beats the no-ask baseline in all cases (average +31.7% SR, +19.9% SPL), e.g. Both Seen SR 70.9 vs 35.2. It collapses without a teacher. Semi-25/75 curricula keep SR within 5.2 points of baseline when the teacher is absent and reach up to 72.1 SR with one. Language feedback is closest to segmentation feedback; binary and noisy feedback degrade performance.
limitations: Training uses perfect ground-truth feedback, which is unrealistic. Noisy segmentation at evaluation lowers SR by 12.4% on average.
The setting is small and synthetic (AI2-THOR kitchens, 7 object types) with a proof-of-concept language feedback study.

Uncertainty metric is a lower bound that assumes perfect memory, so vapid and insignificant asks appear high. Semi-present agents fall short of the always-present agent when a teacher is present (SR drop of at least 7.7).
